findings.title: Reporting/aggregation not updated for multi-currency expenses
findings.description: add_expense now allows storing expenses in any currency, but the PR description states reporting is unchanged. Any report or summary function that sums amount_cents across a user's expenses will now silently add together amounts in different currencies (e.g. USD cents + EUR cents) as if they were the same unit, producing meaningless/incorrect totals. Multi-currency support needs either currency-aware aggregation or explicit conversion before this feature is safe to ship.

findings.title: currency parameter is unvalidated
findings.description: Unlike category, the new currency argument is inserted directly into the database with no validation. Callers can pass an empty string, lowercase codes, non-ISO-4217 strings, or arbitrarily long text, leading to inconsistent/garbage data in the currency column (e.g. 'usd' vs 'USD' would be treated as different currencies by any downstream grouping logic).

findings.title: No constraint on currency column values
findings.description: The currency column has no CHECK constraint or length limit, so combined with the missing application-level validation, the database can end up storing arbitrary strings as currency codes rather than valid 3-letter ISO codes.

findings.title: Missing tests for invalid currency and reporting impact
findings.description: The only new test verifies a valid currency round-trips correctly. There is no test asserting invalid/empty currency values are rejected, and no test covering how existing reporting/summary functions behave when expenses use mixed currencies, which is exactly the scenario this feature introduces.
